scope: Independent source-diff and synthetic HTML-structure review of shared renderer changes only. No mathematical audit/source/lesson payload reassessment. No repo edits.

findings.description: Each binding now passes its own escaped source comparison, boundary, current audit details, legacy debt and repair overlays into its own rendered lesson. Original source statement/formulas remain once at the source-card level, and obligations retain the same labels and admission logic after lessons. No content or status logic was dropped.

The optional keyword-only source_comparison argument defaults empty, preserving all existing callers. Required actual hypotheses, notation/conventions, natural proof steps, examples, full Lean disclosures/helpers, scope boundary and every provenance subsection remain rendered. The main statement and proof disclosures are closed after natural steps; provenance is now visibly shared by standalone/module/publication lesson consumers, with no optimisation special case.

Legacy debt is independently rendered alongside a current audit, with wording explicitly refusing retrospective certification. Pending fallback remains available. This correctly distinguishes historical evidence debt from the current-version verdict.

The test extracts a lesson through the first closing article tag. semantic_details can emit nested repair articles, so a repair-bearing lesson is truncated before its provenance and the check fails for the wrong reason. Use a balanced HTML tree or balanced article extraction scoped by data-authored-declaration, and include a nested-repair fixture. This is a regression-test robustness issue; the renderer itself preserves nested repair content correctly.
findings.resolution: Independently inspected updated test: slice ends at next top-level proof-reader start (or page end), retaining nested repair articles. The independently run tree fixture already confirms actual renderer association and nested-repair preservation.

findings.description: assertNotIn(<details open) does not detect the ordinary attribute order <details class=... open>. Inspect actual Lean details nodes for an open attribute. The current emitted Lean disclosures are correctly closed; this observation concerns future-regression sensitivity.
findings.resolution: Independently inspected updated test: assertNotRegex now detects an open attribute after arbitrary details attributes. Current output remains closed in synthetic tree checks.

findings.description: Removing audit_id only from the copied test fixture correctly isolates historical debt admission when current real reviews are now attached. This preserves the negative test meaning without changing production audit data.

validation.method: Executed /private/tmp/andi_reader_synthetic.py with /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14; mocked publication inputs and declarations, so no mathematical audit records were loaded as test data.
cases: exactly one correctly keyed comparison inside each authored article
two same-declaration main Lean details with no open attribute
main Lean statement then proof then own comparison then visible provenance
historical debt and current audit both present
standalone render_unit caller with default empty comparison
no top-level h1 in embedded source card
validation.runtime_note: The default python3 could not import the existing astis_site.py because its Python version rejects a pre-existing newer f-string syntax. Rerunning with installed Python 3.14 passed; this was not introduced by the reviewed diff.

minimality: Accepted: two shared renderer files and one regression-test file change presentation without authoring duplicate mathematics or introducing library-specific paths. Visible provenance intentionally affects all render_unit consumers, as requested.
limitations: No browser rendering or visual QA was performed by this reviewer; root owns those checks.
No full site build or full repository gate was performed by this reviewer.
Existing per-step Lean mini-disclosures remain adjacent to individual proof steps; both main exact Lean disclosures follow the complete mathematical step sequence.
Existing page-wide publication validator remains weaker than parser-based synthetic association checks. The two concrete regression-test findings were addressed in the current diff.
